note: Attacker-controlled stdin line is copied into buff and parsed as an H3 index string.
The parser accepts the raw string and converts it to a 64-bit H3Index value without validating that the text is a canonical cell index.
The parsed index is passed into the k-ring computation used by the vulnerable candidate.
gridDiskUnsafe forwards the attacker-controlled origin directly into the distance-based ring walker.
The ring walker derives neighbors from the supplied origin before any validation of the digit layout, so malformed digits can influence neighbor traversal.

code: Returns INVALID_DIGIT if the cells are not neighbors.
note: Neighbor traversal depends on digit-to-direction logic; invalid digits can propagate into INVALID_DIGIT and then into code paths that assume a valid direction.

The root cause is that malformed H3 digits are only rejected by validation, but traversal helpers read them directly and can reach invalid-direction handling that leads to the crash in the vulnerable target.
